status: Full complex H-minus-one normalized Dirichlet characteristic constructed; rough boundary operator zero criterion and source Dirichlet estimate remain open
results: The normalized classical scalar Dirichlet characteristic is the actual terminal position of the Hill IVP with initial position zero and derivative one. Its fixed first-order initial vector, exact constant shift and free zero-energy value one are proved.

The L2 characteristic uses the actual physical L2 fundamental solution. Its entire even frequency dependence is proved by physical continuous-potential comparison and L2 density. Entire square descent gives joint norm analyticity in energy and L2 potential, including zero, with the exact scalar normalization and constant-shift law.

A FIXED invertible state map P(v)=(v1+v2,i(v1-v2)) transforms the quasi-Hill equation into the existing first-order system at frequency -(lambda+1)/2 with source entries -i*u+(lambda-1)/2 and i*u+(lambda-1)/2. These entries are affine in energy and lift; there is no spectral division or excluded zero energy.

The affine source gives actual L2 solution curves jointly analytic in energy and input in the full uniform curve norm. Every prescribed scalar initial state is retained exactly. Compatible continuous representatives recover the independent quasi-Hill IVP.

For EVERY original complex H1 input, the energy-affine source has the physical continuous representative of its Sobolev synthesis. This proves complete solution and Dirichlet normalization agreement without a caller-supplied compatibility hypothesis.

Continuous C1 Miura profiles give the independently normalized physical Hill Dirichlet characteristic by the actual scalar equation and IVP uniqueness. H1 Fourier density extends the comparison to all original H1 inputs. Every rough L2 Miura input whose image is L2 has the actual L2 Dirichlet characteristic, including exact physical energy translations.

Analytic shifted Miura charts define a single Dirichlet characteristic on ALL complex unit-period H-minus-one potentials. Chart independence, independence of inverse branch and mass, joint entire energy/potential dependence, exact physical L2 agreement and uniqueness of the continuous L2 extension are proved.

The complete rough Miura identity and constant-energy translation identity hold for every complex L2 lift and H-minus-one image. In particular ANY literal shifted Miura lift represents the same full H-minus-one Dirichlet characteristic, with no zero-energy exception. The free zero-energy value is exactly one.
qualifications: The H-minus-one family is a proved analytic extension of the normalized physical L2 scalar IVP, not an assumed spectral characteristic or a function specified by a supplied root list.

Its zero set has NOT YET been identified with the full rough Dirichlet operator spectrum. No canonical Dirichlet labeling, rough Dirichlet multiplicity formula, interlacing theorem or source 2.1(ii) estimate is claimed in this milestone.

The continuous comparison in QuasiHillL2Energy accepts the explicit physical-class equality; QuasiHillL2Sobolev PROVES that equality on every original H1 input. The later Miura comparison and H-minus-one chart construction do not retain that equality as an unproved hypothesis.

Original unit-period coefficients and their derivative symbol 2*pi*i*n are retained by the existing physical source maps. The independently verified L2 Hill characteristic uses the original period-two even insertion and unit physical IVP interval.

The fixed-basis realization is affine in energy and L2 profile. The complete scalar initial position/quasi-derivative is retained even at zero energy; no artificial zero is introduced by multiplication or division by frequency.
Source Theorem 2.2(i)-(iii), Lemma 2.21 and all Appendix B clauses remain proved. Main Theorems 1.1,1.3,1.4,5.1,5.9 remain unproved and the goal remains active.
essential_remaining: Identify zeros of this full rough Dirichlet characteristic with the actual original H-minus-one Dirichlet boundary operator, with its exact physical domain and multiplicities.

Construct the original canonical Dirichlet eigenvalue labels and prove their comparison to the actual periodic/antiperiodic midpoint, including the weighted endpoint asymptotic estimate and local boundedness in source Theorem 2.1(ii).

Complete the required low simplicity/interlacing and boundary parity identifications. Construct the original KdV Birkhoff maps and the actual H-minus-one smooth-approximation flow; all five main article theorems remain unproved.
